elements.quote: Searches of 8 bibliographic databases were performed to systematically review the evidence on the prevalence, risk factors, clinical characteristics, and prognosis of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection among HCWs.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the report as a systematic review of the evidence.

elements.quote: to systematically review the evidence on the prevalence, risk factors, clinical characteristics, and prognosis of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection among HCWs
elements.reason: The abstract states the objective of reviewing prevalence, risk factors, clinical characteristics, and prognosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection among HCWs.

elements.quote: A total of 97 studies (all published in 2020) met the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions that studies 'met the inclusion criteria' but does not state what those criteria (or exclusions) were.

elements.quote: Searches of 8 bibliographic databases were performed
elements.reason: The abstract mentions searching 8 databases but does not name them or report when each source was last searched (dates appear only in the Methods, text_3).
The abstract contains no statement of how risk of bias or study quality was assessed; quality assessment methods appear only in the Methods section.
The abstract does not describe the methods used to present or synthesize results (e.g., random-effects pooling, meta-analysis methods); such details are only in the Methods (text_5).

elements.quote: A total of 97 studies (all published in 2020) met the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (97) but not the number of participants, nor study characteristics beyond publication year.

elements.quote: The estimated prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection from HCWs' samples, using reverse transcription - polymerase chain reaction and the presence of antibodies, was 11% (95% confidence interval (CI): 7 , 15) and 7% (95% CI: 4, 11), respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for the main outcomes (prevalence by test, most affected personnel, symptoms, asymptomatic proportion, severe complications, deaths), though without per-outcome study/participant counts.

elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted, and the abstract reports pooled summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals for the main outcomes.

elements.quote: Anosmia, fever, and myalgia were the only symptoms associated with HCW SARS-CoV-2 positivity.

elements.quote: Currently, there is no clarity regarding the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among HCWs according to specific clinical settings... Furthermore, it is unknown whether the clinical characteristics and outcomes of HCWs may be different from those of the general population
elements.reason: The introduction describes existing knowledge (CDC case reports, transmission by asymptomatic carriers) and explicitly identifies uncertainties regarding prevalence, clinical characteristics, and outcomes in HCWs.

elements.quote: Therefore, characterizing SARS-CoV-2 infection within HCWs is critical for achieving optimal control of the pandemic. With the present systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to identify, analyze, and quantify the prevalence, risk factors, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of COVID-19 among HCWs.
elements.reason: The importance of the review is explained (critical for pandemic control, designing preventive measures) and the review aim is stated.

elements.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review quantifying the burden of COVID-19 among HCWs.
elements.reason: The authors state this is the first systematic review on the topic, explaining the need for the current review; no previous review needed citation.
This is a review of prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes, not of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action is required.
The review does not evaluate complex interventions or delivery contexts, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.reason: Effect measures are specified for prevalence (proportions via double arcsine transformation) and for dichotomous risk factors (odds ratios), but no effect measure is explicitly stated for other outcomes such as clinical characteristics or symptoms association, so coverage is not complete for every outcome.

No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (e.g., what constitutes a large prevalence or OR) or their rationale are reported in the retrieved evidence; only significance thresholds (P<0.05, P=0.01) are given, which is not the same as effect-size interpretation thresholds.
No methods for re-expressing results using another effect measure are described in the retrieved evidence.
